name: Radboud Encouragement Scholarship
requiredDocuments: Online application for admission to an English-taught Master's programme in the OSIRIS Application system, indicating that you wish to apply for the Radboud Encouragement Scholarship
Two reference letters (the same letters used for the Master's application may be reused)
Curriculum vitae (the same CV used for the Master's application may be reused)
A scholarship motivation letter — must be a DIFFERENT letter than the Master's programme motivation letter, explaining why you need this scholarship in order to be able to attend Radboud University

timeline.deadline: Submit in OSIRIS by 31 January 2025 23:59 CEST; application must be COMPLETE by 14 February 2025 23:59 CEST
timeline.notes: Anchored to 2026-06: documenting the fully-documented 2025-2026 cycle. As of 2026-06 the 2026-2027 cycle has CLOSED and the live Encouragement page sits behind a Surfconext login wall (returns HTTP 403/login stub). The sibling Radboud Scholarship Programme page shows the equivalent 2026-2027 dates (submit by 31 January 2026 23:59 CET, complete by 14 February 2026 23:59 CET, decision before mid-April 2026). Studies start 1 September. Verify the next cycle's exact dates on the official page when it reopens.

benefits: Full tuition fee waiver for the nominal duration of the Master's programme
Living-costs allowance of €13,200 (the IND-set amount, January 2025, for 2025-2026)
Costs of visa and residence permit
Health insurance and liability insurance for the stay in the Netherlands (Aon Student Insurance)
mustKnow: Two-step process: scholarship selection and Master's admission are SEPARATE processes — admission to the programme does NOT imply selection for the scholarship. You must already be (or be in the process of being) fully admitted to an English-taught Master's starting 1 September.

Need-based + merit: you must declare you do NOT have sufficient funds or access to grants/loans to finance your studies at Radboud University, AND the faculty selection committee makes a selection based on academic qualities after the scholarship motivation letter has been judged.
The scholarship motivation letter must be a SEPARATE, distinct letter from your Master's-programme motivation letter, explaining specifically why you need the scholarship.

Eligibility requires a Bachelor's degree obtained OUTSIDE the Netherlands and no prior Dutch degrees/education (exchange programmes that were part of your foreign Bachelor's are excluded from this restriction); you must hold a non-EU/non-EEA passport and not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee.
Erasmus Mundus Master's programmes and joint-degree Master's programmes are NOT eligible — only standard English-taught Radboud Master's.

Genuinely fully funded (tuition + €13,200 living allowance + insurance) — do NOT confuse it with the separate Radboud Scholarship Programme, which is PARTIAL (reduces tuition to about €2,694 and does NOT cover living costs).
Very limited slots: for 2025-2026 only 11 Encouragement Scholarships were available across faculties (Medical Sciences 6; Arts, Management, Philosophy/Theology, Science, Social Sciences 1 each).
For a two-year Master's, second-year funding is conditional: you must pass all first-year courses to qualify for the grant again in the second year.
duration: Nominal duration of the Master's programme (typically 1-2 years)
eligibleNationalities: Applicants from all non-EU/non-EEA countries (no closed bilateral list). Must hold a non-EU/non-EEA passport and not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee. Bangladesh is eligible. Erasmus Mundus and joint-degree programmes are excluded.
languageRequirements: Must meet the English language proficiency requirement of the chosen Master's programme (typically IELTS/TOEFL; exact band set per programme).
monthlyStipend: Living-costs allowance of €13,200 for 2025-2026 (annual, IND-set; not paid as a separate monthly stipend amount in the official text)
renewalConditions: For a two-year Master's, you must pass all first-year courses to qualify for the grant again in the second year.
